overview:
### Release pipeline: npm trusted publishing (OIDC). Difficulty: 3/5

This change removes the long-lived `NPM_TOKEN` secret from the release flow. The package is now published to npm with **trusted publishing**: the workflow's GitHub OIDC identity (`id-token: write`) is exchanged for a short-lived publish credential, which works because the trusted publisher on npmjs.com names `release.yml`. The npm publish step now runs **before** the GitHub Release is created, and setup-node moves from Node 22 to Node 24 (which ships an npm version that supports OIDC). The header comments now describe a manual bump, commit, annotated tag and push process in place of `npm version`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["git push tag vX.Y.Z"] --> B["release.yml: build binaries + checksums"]
    B --> C["generate /tmp/changelog.md"]
    C --> D["setup-node (Node 24, registry.npmjs.org)"]
    D --> E["npm publish --access public --provenance"]
    E --> F{"OIDC token exchange accepted by npm?"}
    F -->|"yes"| G["package published with provenance"]
    F -->|"no"| H["job fails, no GitHub Release created"]
    G --> I["gh release create + upload dist/ assets"]
    class D,E,F,H chg
    classDef chg fill:#d6ffd9,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#111
```

**Riskiest area:** the new publish-then-release order. npm versions are immutable, so if `gh release create` fails after a successful `npm publish`, the npm package is live with no GitHub Release or binaries. A rerun of the job will then fail at the publish step. Also check that `prepublishOnly` (tests) can run in this job's environment and that the npm bundled with Node 24 meets the minimum version for OIDC trusted publishing.
